facts.fact: President Ruto announced the Digital Superhighway's 100,000km national fibre target in November 2022 for universal broadband availability over five years, with a deadline of 2027 that the 2 September 2026 report says is still ahead, and no successor named.

The Digital Superhighway fibre programme is funded through the Universal Service Fund, with the CA and ICT Authority initially signing a Sh5 billion agreement covering 19 counties, and Kenya Power had received Sh940.6 million by June 2025 for design, supply and installation, per the Daily Nation.
ICT Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo said on 2 September 2026 that 37,000km of the 100,000km fibre target serving 53,000 government facilities had been laid, leaving 63,000km.
